newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish June bond volume down yr/yr, stock trade up.
newsitem.headline: Danish June bond volume down yr/yr, stock trade up.

text.p: Danish bond turnover was a nominal 465.9 billion crowns in June, down 15 percent compared to June 1996 but up seven percent from May 1997, the Copenhagen Stock Exchange said on Thursday.
Average daily trading volume totalled 23.3 billion crowns in June 1997, up from May's 21.9 billion.
Government bonds had turnover during the month of 279.9 billion crowns and standard mortgage bonds accounted for 144.2 billion. Repo trading was 1,840 billion crowns, up 19 percent from May.
The average true yield dropped 21 basis points, to 6.20 percent, the exchange said.
Share trading reached a market value of 28.4 billion crowns in June, up 63 percent from June last year and 38 percent higher than May 1997.
Average daily volume was 1.4 billion crowns, compared to 999 million in June 1996 and 1.0 billion in May 1997.
Sophus Berendsen was the month's most-traded share, with turnover of 3.3 billion crowns, followed by BG Bank with 2.8 billion.
